messages.subject: Parsimonious VECM
parts:
Hi,
 
First of all, thank you for the very useful package!
 
I am using it to obtain full information maximum likelihood VECM estimates such as the following.
Restrict.VECM<-VECM(Data, lag=1, include="const", estim="ML", r=3)
However, in order to achieve a parsimonious model I want to first estimate a general first-order VECM, and then reduce it by excluding variables that are insignificant at a particular threshold level (say 5%).
 
I then intend to predict forward using this parsimonious model:
predict(Restrict.VECM,n.ahead=1)[ ,1]
As I am re-estimating a large number of times, is there any functionality in tsdyn, to reduce the VECM variables in such a manner?
 
Thanks in advance,
Davina

messages.author: 8c45483022d450d5
messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] Parsimonious VECM
parts:
Dear Davina

it is not very clear to me what you would like to do. Especially, what do you mean by *reducing the model"? Do you want to reduce the number of lags, or, for a given lag, restrict some coefficients to be zero? And are you speaking here about the short term lag coefficient, or the cointegrating alpha/beta? You can impose a few restrictions on the pi matrix with tsDyn, but vars/urca has more features for that specific purpose, including a large choice of tests on the parameters, as well as larger possibilities to estimate restricted models.

Best

Matthieu
